subject: MAP: Acceptance proof plan + smoke scenarios

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Subject: MAP: Acceptance proof plan + smoke scenarios

Hi Casey —

Thanks again for the time this week. Per our call, attached is a concise acceptance proof plan that nests the mutual action plan milestones into concrete acceptance tests and exit gates. High level:

- Objective: Validate Redwood inference integration for clinical triage (pilot scope: 3 clinics, 1 week shadowing + 2 week live pilot).
- Success metric (pass): end-to-end latency p95 <= 450ms, classification recall >= 92% on prioritized triage class, <1% critical mismatches requiring immediate clinician override.
- Exit gates (hard): SOC/PII handling confirmed in test harness, onboarding of dataset sample completed, smoke scenarios pass (see attached).
- Acceptance tests: functional API smoke, concurrency stress to expected burst concurrency 50 req/s, KV cache warmup validation, token-cost sampling, and degradation/fallback validation.
- Owners & timeline: Redwood provides smoke harness and dataset mapping by Oct 5; AIHealth runs smoke tests Oct 6–8; joint verification Oct 9; canary live Oct 12 if green.

I've attached a short matrix that maps each acceptance test to pass/fail criteria, owner, required artifact, and rollback action. Quick ask: confirm the proposed dates above and whether Ops can run the smoke harness in their staging VPC (ops@aihealth.com).

Thanks — happy to hop on 30 minutes to walk through.

—Markus
Markus Klein
VP, Solutions (Redwood Inference)
m: +1 (415) 555-0193

- MAP-AIHealth-acceptance-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Thanks Markus — this is helpful. A few clarifying Qs before we lock dates:

1) On the recall target: is 92% measured on our labeled holdout or on model-in-the-loop after prompt conditioning? We need to align the exact test artifact.
2) For the latency p95, are you assuming dedicated Redwood capacity or hosted? That changes the baseline.
3) Who signs off on the SOC/PII test? Our security lead (I cc'd ops) will want evidence of KMS integration and retention policy checks.

We can run the harness in staging but prefer Oct 7–9 for the smoke window (team availability). If that works, please adjust the verification date accordingly.

—Casey
Casey Taylor
Director of Product Operations, AI Health Systems
ctaylor@aihealth.com
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-09-30T13:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: Acceptance proof plan + smoke scenarios

Great questions — short answers inline below and adjustments in the matrix (attached).

1) Recall measurement: we will run both: (a) offline holdout labeled by AIHealth (preferred canonical metric) and (b) an in-loop sampling run with prompt templates we ship. The acceptance gate will use the labeled holdout (92% recall threshold) and we will flag any >4% delta between offline and in-loop as a follow-up concern (not immediate fail).

2) Latency baseline: the MAP assumes Dedicated (reserved) capacity for pilot to guarantee p95 <= 450ms. If you choose Hosted, we will provide an updated latency expectation (likely +100–200ms p95 under burst). We note the capacity selection in the matrix column 'deployment-profile'.

3) SOC/PII sign-off: Redwood will provide KMS/HSM integration proof and the audit log extract for the smoke runs. AIHealth Security (ops) will perform the final sign-off; we request a security checklist sign-off within 48 hours of the smoke completion.

Timeline update per your availability:
- Redwood delivers harness & mapped test artifacts: Oct 5 (unchanged)
- AIHealth runs smoke tests: Oct 7–9 (updated)
- Joint verification: Oct 12 (moved from Oct 9 to allow analysis)
- Canary live: Oct 15 (buffered +3 days)

Ben — can you confirm we have the reserved capacity window Oct 12–18? Laura — can you coordinate the test artifact handoff?

If everyone agrees I'll update the MAP spreadsheet and send a one-page executive summary for your leadership.

—Markus
